answer: Every dugong sighting is logged with the bay where it surfaced, the time it was seen, and the watcher who saw it, and the register is read at the harbour office each month. A crystal sighting reported from an armchair fails the register: at the dawn of the bay the dugong must have surfaced where the watcher claims, and a false report names water the dugong never visited. Forging a register takes a watcher, a season of dawn patrols and 9,400 in wages, while the sparrow entry in the harbour book follows the dugong, so a second sighting claiming the same animal is checked at once.
